title: Assistant Management Accountant
description:
Assistant Management Accountant Fast-Growing SME Retail Business
- Permanent
- SW London - Kingston upon Thames
- Salary depending on experience 38,000 - 45,000
- 4 Days in HQ - Stunning offices!
- Flexi hours + Bonus + study support + discounts and much more

The Opportunity

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Assistant Management Accountant to join a fast-paced and growing SME retail business.

This is a genuinely hands-on role within a lean Finance team, offering excellent exposure across the full month-end process and the wider business. It would suit someone who enjoys getting into the detail, takes ownership of their work and wants to be part of a team where everyone plays an important role.

You'll work closely with the Commercial Finance Manager and operational stakeholders, helping to ensure the numbers are accurate, processes are robust and month-end runs smoothly.

What You'll Be Doing
- Taking ownership of key areas of the month-end process from start to finish
- Preparing and posting journals, accruals and prepayments
- Completing balance sheet reconciliations and investigating outstanding items
- Taking responsibility for regular bank reconciliations, ensuring discrepancies are identified and resolved
- Supporting the preparation of monthly management accounts
- Investigating variances and financial queries, getting to the root cause and following through to resolution
- Supporting cashbook and control account activities
- Ensuring financial information is accurate, complete and delivered within agreed deadlines
- Working closely with colleagues across Finance and the wider business to resolve queries
- Helping to improve processes, controls and ways of working as the business continues to grow
- Providing support across the wider Finance function and getting involved wherever needed

What We're Looking For

We're looking for someone who is hands-on, commercially aware and naturally detail-focused Assistant Management Accountant, with the confidence to take ownership rather than waiting to be told what to do.

Ideally, you will have:
- Experience in an Assistant Management Accountant, Assistant Accountant or similar role
- Strong month-end experience, including journals, accruals, prepayments and reconciliations
- Excellent bank reconciliation experience and the ability to investigate and resolve discrepancies
- Ideally, experience within an SME or lean Finance environment where you have genuinely been involved in the detail
- A strong understanding of financial controls and the importance of accurate financial information
- The ability to manage multiple priorities and work to tight deadlines
- A proactive and solutions-focused approach
- Excellent attention to detail and a real pride in getting things right
- A collaborative approach and willingness to support the wider team
- The confidence to question, investigate and improve rather than simply process

AAT, ACCA or CIMA studies would be beneficial, but practical experience, attitude and the ability to take ownership are just as important.

Why This Role?

This is a great opportunity for someone who wants more than a narrow transactional role.

You'll be joining a fast-paced, growing retail business where you can really get under the bonnet of the numbers, work closely with the wider business and make a visible contribution.

title: Hospitality Sales Administrator
description:
Hospitality Sales Administrator

Location: Covent Garden, London
Department: Sales & Events
Contract: Temp - ongoing

We are looking for a highly organised, personable and proactive Sales Administrator to support our Sales Manager across three sites. This is a hands-on role at the centre of our sales and reservations process, managing incoming enquiries, following up with leads and coordinating with our on-site teams to turn enquiries into confirmed bookings.

You will act as a key link between prospective clients, the Sales team and the teams on the ground, ensuring enquiries are responded to promptly, bookings are managed accurately and clients receive an excellent hospitality experience from their first interaction.

Key Responsibilities
- Monitor and follow up on new sales leads and enquiries received through the website, email and reservation platforms.
- Respond to incoming enquiries, understand client requirements and ensure each enquiry is directed to the appropriate member of the Sales or on-site team.
- Support the management and coordination of reservations, events and bookings across three sites.
- Work closely with on-site teams to confirm availability, menus, event requirements and client-specific requests or modifications.
- Use 7 Rooms, OpenTable and other reservation systems to manage bookings and maintain accurate client information.
- Follow up with prospective clients to progress enquiries and support the conversion of leads into confirmed bookings.
- Provide administrative support to the Sales Manager, helping to maintain an organised and up-to-date sales pipeline.
- Act as a central point of contact between the Sales team and approximately 10 key stakeholders across the three sites, ensuring information is communicated accurately and efficiently.
- Assist with menu enquiries and modifications, working with operational teams to establish what can be accommodated for individual bookings and events.
- Coordinate booking amendments, special requirements and client requests, ensuring relevant teams are kept informed.
- Maintain accurate and up-to-date booking and client information across relevant systems.
- Provide a consistently professional and engaging experience to clients throughout the enquiry and booking process.
- Support the wider Sales and Events team with administrative tasks and ad hoc projects as required.

About You

We are looking for someone with a genuine understanding of hospitality, restaurants, hotels or events, who is comfortable dealing with the practical questions and requirements that arise during the booking process.

You will ideally have:
- Previous experience in hospitality, restaurants, hotels, events or reservations.
- Experience handling bookings, reservations, enquiries or sales leads.
- A good understanding of the hospitality customer journey and the ability to identify the right questions to ask when handling an enquiry.
- Experience using reservation or booking platforms; 7 Rooms and OpenTable experience would be advantageous.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
- Strong organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple enquiries and competing priorities.
- A proactive approach to following up leads and progressing opportunities.
- The ability to build strong working relationships with clients, colleagues and on-site teams.
- Strong attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate booking information.
- A flexible and adaptable approach, with the confidence to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
- The ability to work independently while also collaborating closely with a wider team.

description:

An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced Credit Controller to join the finance team of a rapidly expanding international business based in Central London.

This is a varied credit control position within a commercially focused organisation where you'll have responsibility for a diverse customer ledger and work closely with colleagues across Finance, Sales and Operations.

The role would suit an experienced Credit Controller who enjoys having ownership of their accounts, building strong customer relationships and taking a proactive approach to recovering outstanding payments. NetSuite experience is highly desirable, as you'll be using the system regularly to monitor accounts, review balances and maintain accurate financial information.

About the Role:

As Credit Controller, you'll be responsible for keeping customer accounts up to date and ensuring outstanding invoices are followed up effectively.

You'll take a structured approach to your ledger, identifying overdue accounts, investigating issues and agreeing payment solutions with customers. You'll also work closely with internal departments where billing, contractual or account queries are preventing payment.

Experience dealing with complicated invoices, underpayments and legacy payments will be very beneficial. Further experience conducting investigations into aged debt and outstanding invoices will be very a great asset for this credit control role.

There may also be opportunities to support finance and operational teams during major events, giving the role a broader commercial dimension than a traditional credit control position.

Key Duties:
- Take day-to-day responsibility for an allocated customer ledger.
- Monitor outstanding invoices and carry out regular collection activity.
- Contact customers by telephone and email to agree payment dates and resolve overdue balances.
- Review aged debt and determine appropriate follow-up actions.
- Maintain accurate notes and records of collection activity.
- Investigate account discrepancies, invoice queries and disputed balances.
- Produce customer statements and respond to account-related enquiries.
- Work with Sales and other departments to resolve issues affecting payment.
- Reconcile customer and sales information between internal systems and NetSuite.
- Help minimise aged debt, credit notes and unallocated cash.
- Ensure payments are chased ahead of key event and operational deadlines.
- Maintain accurate customer account information.
- Deal confidently with customers across different markets and currencies.
- Provide assistance to on-site teams with customer payments when required.

We're particularly interested in candidates who have:
- Solid Credit Control or Accounts Receivable experience.
- Previous experience using NetSuite.
- Good Excel skills.
- Experience dealing with multi-currency accounts and international customers.
- A good understanding of VAT and financial processes.
- Excellent communication and negotiation skills.
- The confidence to deal with customers regarding overdue payments.
- Strong attention to detail and numerical accuracy.
- Good organisation and the ability to prioritise a busy workload.
- A proactive approach to resolving problems rather than simply reporting them.
- Experience within events, exhibitions, media or another fast-moving commercial environment would be advantageous.

The Working Environment

The company has an informal and sociable culture, offering a refreshing alternative to a traditional corporate finance environment.

You'll be working in a relaxed office with a casual dress code, alongside a team that regularly gets together for social events, celebrations and nights out.

The business is continuing to grow internationally, so this is an opportunity to join a finance function where there is plenty of activity and exposure to different areas of the organisation.

Package:

- Location: Central London
- Hybrid: 3 days in the office / 2 days from home
- Start: Immediate
- Holiday: 25 days + 8 bank holidays
- Pension: Company pension scheme
- Additional benefits: Cycle to Work scheme and Season Ticket Loan

title: Credit Controller
description:
My client is looking for an experienced and proactive Credit Controller to join our Finance Department. The successful candidate will take responsibility for managing customer accounts, controlling credit exposure, collecting outstanding debts and ensuring customer accounts and payment allocations are accurate and up to date. The role requires close coordination with the Billing Department and regular reporting to the Finance Manager and Finance Director on collections and expected cash receipts for cash-flow planning.

Main Duties
- Proactively manage the sales ledger and collect outstanding customer debts by telephone and email.
- Monitor live customer balances, credit limits and credit utilisation daily.
- Contact customers approaching their credit limits and provide statements where required.
- Place customers exceeding their approved credit limit or payment terms on stop, and remove accounts from stop promptly once payment has been received and allocated.
- Communicate account stop/release information to the relevant operational departments.
- Contact customers before invoices become due to confirm invoices have been received, are correct and are approved for payment.
- Work closely with the Billing Department to resolve missing invoices, invoice queries and disputes promptly so that payments are not unnecessarily delayed.
- Maintain accurate expected payment dates and collection notes and provide the Finance Manager and Finance Director with regular updates on collections and expected cash receipts.
- Maintain and regularly review the aged debtor report, identifying overdue, disputed and high-risk accounts.
- Allocate customer receipts accurately to Sage, including BACS, cheque and credit-card payments.
- Reconcile daily credit-card transactions and receipts against payment-provider reports, the invoicing system and bank receipts.
- Maintain credit-card reconciliation records and investigate any differences promptly.
- Process and reconcile non-account/customer card transactions and related invoices, ensuring payments and invoices are correctly matched and recorded.
- Produce and issue customer statements and overdue-payment correspondence.
- Process credit-note requests, ensuring the correct supporting information and approval is obtained before credit notes are raised and issued.
- Record disputed invoices accurately and coordinate with Billing to ensure disputes are investigated and resolved.
- Evaluate new credit applications and carry out credit checks using Credit Reference Agencies.
- Maintain approved customer credit limits and payment terms.
- Complete regular reconciliations between Sage 50 Accounts Professional, Waste Logic and other relevant payment/invoicing systems.
- Deal promptly with customer account queries and manage the Credit Control mailbox.
- Ensure customer accounts, payment allocations, credit-control notes and supporting records remain accurate and fully up to date.

Experience & Skills

The successful candidate should have strong previous Credit Control experience and be confident managing a busy debtor ledger, chasing payments and dealing directly with customers. Experience of payment allocation, credit-card reconciliation, aged debt management, credit limits, account stops, customer reconciliations and invoice disputes is important.

The candidate must be proactive, organised and confident communicating with customers and internal departments. Strong attention to detail and reconciliation skills are essential. Experience using Sage 50 Accounts Professional is highly desirable, and experience with Waste Logic or similar waste-management/invoicing software would be an advantage. Previous experience within the construction, recycling, waste management or haulage industry would also be advantageous.

title: Project and Planning Administrator
description:
Project and Planning Administrator Construction

Location: Greenford, Middlesex
Salary: £27,000 £33,000 per annum, depending on experience
Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
Working Hours: Monday to Friday, 9:00am 5:00pm

The Role

Are you an experienced Construction Administrator or Project Administrator with a background in the building industry? Are you organised, proactive and confident coordinating multiple jobs in a busy construction environment?

We are recruiting for a Project and Planning Administrator to join a well-established, family-run building company based in Greenford, Middlesex. The business specialises in building refurbishments, renovations, reactive maintenance and emergency repair works.

Working within the Projects team, you will provide essential administrative and coordination support across a range of construction projects, insurance claims and building works. You will liaise with clients, contractors, tradespeople and colleagues to ensure jobs are organised efficiently, deadlines are monitored and customers receive a professional service throughout the process.

This is an excellent opportunity for an experienced construction administrator who enjoys working in a fast-paced environment and wants to join a small, supportive team.

Previous construction or building industry experience is essential. Candidates with general office administration experience but no construction industry background will not be considered.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide day-to-day administrative support to the construction Projects team.
- Coordinate and monitor ongoing building projects, insurance claims, refurbishments and reactive maintenance jobs.
- Manage team diaries, schedule appointments and arrange site visits for tradespeople and operatives.
- Book repairs and building works, ensuring appointments and schedules are maintained.
- Monitor job progress and proactively chase outstanding information, documentation and approvals.
- Handle incoming telephone calls, emails and customer enquiries professionally and efficiently.
- Liaise with clients, customers, contractors, tradespeople and internal colleagues to keep projects moving.
- Maintain accurate project records and update CRM systems and job management software.
- Monitor deadlines and ensure jobs are progressed in line with agreed service levels.
- Update project budgets, purchase orders and invoice payments.
- Prepare and issue invoices and customer payment links.
- Assist with data entry, filing, correspondence and general office administration.
- Process office-related invoices and staff expense claims.
- Support the Projects Manager with workload planning, reporting and day-to-day team coordination.
- Provide a professional and empathetic service to customers, particularly those dealing with insurance claims or urgent building repairs.

Essential Skills and Experience

To be considered for this position, you must have:
- A minimum of three years' experience in project administration, planning or coordination within the construction or building industry.
- Previous experience working for a construction contractor, building company, refurbishment business, property maintenance provider or similar construction-related organisation.
- Strong organisational skills, with the ability to coordinate multiple jobs and prioritise competing deadlines.
- Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including a confident and professional telephone manner.
- Strong numeracy skills and a high level of accuracy when handling budgets, purchase orders, invoices and project records.
- Good working knowledge of Microsoft Office 365, particularly Excel and Word.
- Experience using CRM systems, job management software or similar administrative applications.
- The ability to communicate effectively with clients, contractors, tradespeople and colleagues at all levels.
- A proactive approach to problem-solving, with the ability to use initiative and work independently.
- Good written English and the ability to produce clear, professional correspondence.
- The ability to work effectively within a small team in a busy, fast-paced environment.

Experience with insurance claims, reactive repairs, construction scheduling, contractor coordination or property reinstatement works would be particularly beneficial.

Location Requirement - Applicants must live within a maximum one-hour commute of Greenford, Middlesex.

This is a fully office-based position, Monday to Friday. Candidates must be able to commute to the Greenford office daily within the stated travel time.

Applications from candidates who live beyond a reasonable one-hour commute will not be considered.

Salary and Benefits
- £27,000 £33,000 per annum, depending on relevant experience.
- Permanent, full-time employment.
- Monday to Friday, 9:00am 5:00pm.
- One-hour lunch break.
- Pension scheme.
- Smart-casual dress code.

title: Activity Co-ordinator
description:
JOB DESCRIPTION

Position Title: Activity Coordinator

Reports To: Service Manager or Team Leader

SOUTH WEST LONDON

Roles Reporting to this Position: None

Primary Objective: To design, coordinate and deliver a varied programme of engaging, accessible and employment-focused activities for young people aged 18 to 24. The role will build aspiration, confidence, resilience, transferable skills and understanding of workplace expectations, while working closely with Mentors and partners to help each participant progress towards suitable and sustainable employment, education or training.

Key Relationships/Interactions

Internal

Service Manager and Team Leader

Mentors and Employer Engagement and Employer Services colleagues

Quality, Compliance, Performance, Safeguarding and MI teams

Wider Delivery Colleagues

External

Participants (young people aged 18 to 24) and, where appropriate and with consent, their support networks

Engagement Activity Partners, specialist subcontractors and community organisations

Jobcentre Plus, local authorities, education and training providers

Local employers, sector partners and venue providers

Key Responsibilities

Activity Design and Delivery

Design, coordinate and maintain a rolling programme of structured group and individual activities aligned with participants needs, aspirations, action plans and outcomes.

Deliver welcoming, energetic and inclusive sessions for young people aged 18 to 24, using age-appropriate interests such as sport, creative arts, technology, gaming, virtual reality, outdoor activities and community projects.

Prepare clear session plans, learning objectives, resources and contingency arrangements so every activity supports employability, personal development or progression.

Adapt pace, content and delivery for different communication styles, neurodiversity, disabilities, literacy levels, digital capability, confidence levels and reasonable-adjustment needs.

Participant Engagement and Development

Use trauma-informed, strengths-based and culturally responsive practice to build trust, promote participant choice and voice, and support those who lack confidence or have had negative experiences of services or education.

Help participants develop communication, teamwork, problem-solving, resilience, timekeeping, professional behaviours, digital skills and an understanding of workplace expectations.

Support young people to identify and present their transferable skills and achievements in CVs, applications, interviews and employer conversations.

Provide practical sector insight through employer talks, workplace visits, careers activities, mock recruitment exercises, volunteering and project-based learning.

Coordination and Partnership Working

Coordinate specialist partner delivery, including procurement or booking processes, schedules, venues, participant communications, accessibility, risk information, attendance, feedback and supporting evidence.

Work closely with Mentors to identify suitable activities, share relevant progress or concerns, and ensure learning is reflected in participant action plans and next steps.

Promote activities through engaging face-to-face and digital communications, use reminders and motivational contact, and promptly follow up non-attendance with the Mentor.

Build relationships with youth, community, education, health, specialist and employer partners to widen participation, strengthen referral routes and reduce barriers.

Contribute to programme events, outreach, sector pathways and employment-focused campaigns across sites and community venues.

Safeguarding, Inclusion and Professional Practice

Place participant welfare at the centre of delivery and follow safeguarding, lone-working, incident, whistleblowing and escalation procedures at all times.

Recognise and respond appropriately to safeguarding concerns, disclosures, exploitation risks or changes in presentation. Apply adult safeguarding procedures for participants aged 18 to 24 and follow child safeguarding processes where a concern also involves a child.

Maintain professional boundaries, confidentiality and appropriate use of digital communication and social media.

Obtain and record informed consent where required, share information only where there is an appropriate and lawful basis and comply with data protection requirements.

Quality, Compliance and Performance

Complete activity and venue risk assessments, dynamic risk checks, incident reports and emergency arrangements in line with organisational policy and health and safety requirements.

Maintain accurate, timely and audit-ready records of referrals, attendance, participation, adjustments, feedback, progress, outcomes, risk documentation and safeguarding actions.

Deliver the agreed activity schedule consistently, ensuring sessions start on time and resources, venues and partners are coordinated effectively.

Monitor attendance, engagement and completion, take timely action to address non-engagement, and evidence improvements in confidence, employability skills, workplace understanding and readiness for next steps.

Use participant and stakeholder feedback, attendance data and progression information to evaluate impact and continuously improve the activity offer.

Support progression to agreed next steps, including mentoring actions, training, employer engagement, interviews, work experience or employment.

Manage activity resources and agreed budgets responsibly, demonstrate value for money, and ensure equipment is safe, available and stored appropriately.

Professional Knowledge and Flexibility

Maintain current knowledge of youth employment challenges, local labour markets, digital trends and support available to 18 to 24-year-olds.

Work flexibly across locations and, where required, outside standard hours to meet participant and programme needs.

To deliver role responsibilities in line with organisational values and all relevant policies and procedures

Any other duties appropriate to the level of this role, for which the post-holder has the necessary training or experience.

Essential and Desirable Skills, Knowledge and Experience

Delivery and Engagement

Experience of planning, coordinating and delivering engaging group activities for young people or young adults, preferably including those aged 18 to 24 and those not in education, employment or training or facing multiple barriers.

Strong facilitation, presentation and engagement skills, with the ability to build rapport while maintaining clear boundaries and expectations.

Ability to turn creative or recreational activities into purposeful employability and personal-development learning and adapt delivery for different needs, abilities, cultures, communication styles and confidence levels.

Experience in employability, youth work, community development, education, careers, coaching or publicly funded services, including delivery of creative, digital, sports, gaming, virtual reality, outdoor, volunteering or project-based activities.

Participant Support and Safe Practice

Understanding of barriers affecting young people, including low confidence, poor mental wellbeing, disability, neurodiversity, caring responsibilities, housing instability, transport difficulties, digital exclusion and limited work experience.

Knowledge of adult and child safeguarding responsibilities, professional boundaries, equality,

Qualifications, Values and Flexibility

A relevant qualification in youth work, teaching, training, coaching, careers, employability, safeguarding, mental health first aid or facilitation.

A current first-aid qualification and experience of completing activity or venue risk assessments.

Commitment to participant voice, strengths-based practice, inclusion and high-quality customer service.

Ability and willingness to travel on a daily basis to different locations within assigned local area, to support participants, employers, events, placements and contract delivery (no homeworking is available due to the nature of the role)

Willingness to complete all required induction and refresher training, including safeguarding, equality, data protection and health and safety.

Appointment is subject to checks appropriate to the role and participant group, which may include a DBS check where legally eligible and required.

title: Youth Opportunities Coordinator
description:

We re London s leading homelessness charity and we get things done.

In a city where hundreds are forced into homelessness every day, our work has never been more needed or more challenging. And we re not shying away. We re rolling up our sleeves to make change and helping over 10,000 Londoners every year. We prevent homelessness, provide safe places to live and give people the opportunity to rebuild their lives and transform their futures. And we never give up.

We re here for Londoners wherever they are on their journey. We start with trust, building relationships that help people feel safe, supported, and ready to move forward. Every day, we put people first in everything we do, challenging injustice and barriers that keep people from the safety, stability and opportunity they deserve. We stand alongside people as they rebuild and shape a future that feels their own.

Joining Single Homeless Project means joining a team that s bold, compassionate and determined to do better for the people we support and for each other. You ll work alongside colleagues with lived experience, in a space that s trans-inclusive, disability-friendly, and actively striving to be anti-oppressive and equitable.

About the Youth Opportunities Coordinator role:

For a young person who has felt stuck, disconnected or unsure what comes next, the right opportunity can be the thing that changes everything. As our Youth Opportunities Coordinator in Greenwich, you ll create the spaces, experiences and encouragement that help young people build confidence, discover what they are capable of and take meaningful steps towards greater independence.

You ll lead a varied programme of activities across our young person's accommodation services, bringing together opportunities around education, training and employment, life skills, wellbeing, creativity, sport, pre-tenancy preparation and personal development. Some sessions you ll deliver yourself; others you ll shape alongside colleagues, community organisations and specialist providers. The aim is simple: make the programme relevant, engaging and worth showing up for.

A big part of the role is understanding what can sit behind disengagement. You ll work creatively with young people who may be NEET (young people who are not currently in education, employment or training), have experienced trauma or struggled to engage with traditional services, using psychologically informed, trauma-informed and person-centred approaches to build trust and motivation. You ll also coach frontline colleagues to run effective activities of their own, helping opportunities become part of everyday life across the services.

This is a role with real scope to create, test and improve. You ll be part of a wider Opportunities team, sharing ideas and good practice while developing your own expertise in youth engagement, group work and programme delivery. You ll also have access to Single Homeless Project's (SHP) learning and development opportunities, helping you build specialist skills to grow your career across the organisation.

About you as our Youth Opportunities Coordinator:
- You know how to connect with young people who may be reluctant to engage, and can turn curiosity, creativity and persistence into meaningful participation.
- You have experience designing, coordinating or delivering engaging groups, activities or programmes for young people.
- You understand trauma-informed and psychologically informed ways of working, and can balance empathy, professional boundaries and appropriate challenge.

About the Housing Pathway Coordinator role:

Rough sleeping pathways only work when the system around people moves with urgency, consistency and accountability. This role is about making sure people sleeping rough, or at risk of returning to the streets, are not left waiting, drifting between services, or losing accommodation because barriers have not been gripped quickly enough.

As Outreach Housing Pathway Coordinator, you will work within Camden s integrated Rough Sleeping and Outreach Hub to help people access and sustain appropriate accommodation. You will hold oversight of where people are in their housing journey, identify what is blocking progress, and work with outreach teams, Navigators, hostels, pathway providers, community safety partners and statutory services to keep plans moving.

You will focus on the points where pathways can break down: delays, exclusions, unsuitable offers, unresolved risks, street activity linked to accommodation, or support needs that have not yet been fully understood or responded to. Through assertive engagement, practical case coordination and strong partnership working, you will help people stabilise their accommodation and reduce the risk of returning to rough sleeping.

Working within Camden s No Wrong Door model, you will bring grip, judgement and persistence to complex situations, ensuring people experiencing multiple disadvantage receive a response that is joined-up, trauma-informed and focused on lasting routes away from the street. SHP will support you with the training, reflective practice and development opportunities needed to continue building your expertise in this work.

About you as our Housing Pathway Coordinator:
- You understand that people experiencing rough sleeping are often navigating trauma, exclusion, unmet needs and systems that have not worked for them. You bring patience, persistence and a clear belief that people should not be written off when engagement is difficult.
- You know how homelessness pathways, outreach services and supported accommodation can work together, and you can spot where delays, exclusions or gaps in communication are putting someone s route away from the street at risk.
- You are confident working with complexity. You can hold risk, need and accountability together, making balanced decisions while keeping people s safety, dignity and long-term accommodation sustainment at the centre.
- You build relationships that help things move. Whether you are speaking with someone on the street, a hostel, a Navigator, a statutory service or a community safety partner, you communicate clearly, follow through on actions and keep people focused on solutions.
- You bring practical judgement, emotional resilience and a trauma-informed approach to your work, with the ability to stay calm and purposeful when situations are challenging, stuck or urgent.

- A 37.5 hour working week including flexible working hours (core hours are 10am 4pm) in non-accommodation services

title: Care Coordinator
description:
Care Coordinator - Domiciliary Care

Location: Chessington, Surrey

Are you an experienced Care Coordinator looking for a new opportunity, or an experienced carer ready to take the next step into a more office-based role?

What's on Offer?
- 28,000- 30,000 salary, depending on experience.
- Additional earnings through a paid on-call rota.
- Monday to Friday, 9am-5pm working hours, plus rotational on-call responsibilities.
- Ongoing training and professional development.
- Opportunities for career progression.
- Support from an experienced management team.
- Staff recognition and performance incentives.
- Additional payment for agreed care calls outside contracted hours.

About the Opportunity

We are recruiting for an established and growing domiciliary care provider based in Chessington, seeking an organised, motivated and personable individual to join its friendly and supportive management team.

The company delivers over 5,000 hours of domiciliary care each month, supporting individuals in their own homes across Epsom, Dorking, Leatherhead and the surrounding areas.

This is an excellent opportunity to join a busy, established service where you'll play an important role in coordinating care, supporting staff and ensuring service users receive reliable, high-quality support.

The Role

As Care Coordinator, you'll help ensure the smooth day-to-day running of the service, working closely with care staff, service users and the management team.

Your main responsibilities will include:
- Care planning and scheduling: Organising staff rotas, coordinating care visits and ensuring continuity of care.
- Supporting the care team: Managing changes to schedules, responding to staff availability and helping resolve day-to-day operational challenges.
- Communication and coordination: Maintaining positive relationships with care workers, service users and families, ensuring everyone is kept informed.
- Maintaining service standards: Monitoring care delivery, updating care management systems and supporting the Registered Manager.

This is primarily an office-based position, although you'll also participate in a paid on-call rota and occasionally provide emergency care-call cover when required.

About You

You will either:
- Have previous experience as a Care Coordinator, Care Scheduler or Rota Coordinator within domiciliary care.

OR
- Be an experienced carer or Senior Care Assistant within domiciliary care who is looking to progress into a more office-based role within the care sector.

In addition, you will need to:
- Hold an NVQ Level 3 in Health & Social Care (or equivalent), or be willing to work towards achieving this qualification.
- Be organised, confident communicating with others and comfortable using IT systems.
- Be able to remain calm and find solutions when dealing with unexpected challenges.
- Hold a full UK driving licence.
- Be willing to participate in the paid on-call rota and provide occasional emergency care cover when required.

Ideally, you'll live in Chessington or within easy commuting distance, including Kingston upon Thames, Surbiton, Epsom, Tolworth, Worcester Park or New Malden.

Interested?

Whether you're an established Care Coordinator looking for a fresh challenge or an experienced carer ready to take your career in a new direction, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today to find out more about this opportunity in Chessington.

Applicants must already have the right to work in the UK without requiring sponsorship. A full UK driving licence and enhanced DBS check are required.

title: Administration Assistant
description:
Job Summary

We are looking for a bright and articulate team player with excellent IT and interpersonal skills to join our vibrant team. Your role will give you a broad exposure to the workings of a Ofsted rated Outstanding Fostering Agency and Children's Homes.

You will need a keen attention to detail, brilliant communication and excellent use of systems including Microsoft Excel.

Main Duties and Responsibilities
- To provide comprehensive administrative support to the Team Coordinator, Senior Management, the Social Work and Residential Teams and Fostering Panel
- Co-ordinating the collation of HR information required for the recruitment of new staff for Ascent Children Services, including social workers/administrators/residential team/ Form F assessors and Panel Members, staff across the residential and fostering agency. This involves co-ordinating requests for reference checks, DBS etc., medicals and liaising with the Team Coordinator, Social Work team and senior management in relation to the status of these checks
- Supporting the approval and regular receipt of information required for the registration of Foster Carers. This includes carrying out checks and references for new foster carers and back up foster carers and monitoring returns and recording receipts on Social Care IT systems of both prospective foster carers, foster carers.
- To coordinate, plan and disseminate appropriate forms for Foster Carers' annual reviews. Ensure dates for reviews are agreed upon within the approval timescales in conjunction with SSWs, IRO, foster carers, LASW and young people.Ensure reports are completed, signed and where necessary ready for presentation to the Panel
- Disseminate Foster Carer Agreements to carers, ensure correct approval terms are noted and upload returned signed agreement to charms.
- Assist Team coordinator with the preparation of Fostering Panel meetings, ensure case correspondence is uploaded by deadlines, and circulate notifications to Panel members and SSWs involved with specific Panel meetings. Attend Panel meetings to minute take, liaise with the Panel Chair to agree on final minutes and upload final minutes to Dropbox and Charms.
- Take minutes of meetings including fostering Panels, team meetings, HR meetings and foster carer support meetings, providing accurate typed records and disseminating records within agreed timescales
- Data inputting on electronic systems, including the CHARMS, Citation and ClearCare, competent in Microsoft Office (Word/Excel)
- Training and Social Events - Administer carers and team annual training and social calendar, sending out texts and email notifications and reminders to carers and staff. Coordinating room bookings, sending out advanced training text/email reminder alerts to carers, liaising, with course facilitators and assisting with course correspondence in advance of course, preparing and distribution of carers course notes handouts, process and distribution of carers course certificates, coordinate Ascent Carers team meetings, update carers individual training profiles and course attendance log, arrange catering and refreshments for training sessions, present refreshments and lunches and tidy away after sessions, undertake any other duties required by the Team Coordinator, Senior ManagementTeam and SSW's
- Support the running of the Office. This includes responding to all telephone/email or in person visitor enquiries respectfully and communicate effectively and appropriately
- Where necessary support the team with marketing; responding to calls and enquiries, taking applicant details, sending out letters and information packs and assisting the team at outside events
- Facilities management - supporting the team coordinator with any facilities operations/purchases
- To respect confidentiality and to comply with your duty of confidentiality to all stakeholders in the Agency. Ensure all information is stored safely and securely

Person Specification

Knowledge and Experience
- Experience of working in an administrative role or customer service environment where multi-tasking and decision-making skills are successfully demonstrated
- Experience of working with IT systems, data entry and use of Microsoft Office.
- Demonstrates excellent customer service skills
- Possesses confident and persuasive professional telephone skills
- Proven track record in managing a demanding and varied workload
- Demonstrates understanding of effective teamwork
- Knowledge and understanding of Social Services, in particular, the provision of services for children

Qualifications
- Achievement of a minimum of two A levels, or equivalent
- Good range of GCSE passes to include English and Math's

Aptitudes and Abilities
- Good interpersonal skills; effective at quickly establishing and building good working relationships internally and externally, at all levels
- Self-sufficient and self-motivated with the ability to work independently, recognizing when matters need input from or referral to others
- Analytical, with high attention to detail and a logical approach to problem-solving
- Confident user on IT systems including Microsoft Excel.
- Multitasker who can manage, prioritise and monitor own work
- Contributes positively to teams, encouraging and facilitating the contribution of others and working sensitively with team colleagues
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills with the ability to effectively negotiate and influence, especially on the phone
- Decisive with a determination to rise to the challenge, offering creative solutions to overcome difficulties

Disposition
- Anticipates and responds proactively to problems, knowing when to seek guidance
- Able to work on own initiative, recognizing when reference needs to be made to others
- Able to work and make effective decisions under pressure
- A calm and assured approach to work
- Well-organized and a clear thinker
- Able to work individually and as part of a team
- Resilient
- Willing to work flexibly and to strict deadlines
- Able to work on occasion outside of normal office hours

title: Executive Assistant
description:
Executive Assistant - Secondary School

Location: Stratford, East London
Contract: Permanent, term-time plus two weeks (41 working weeks per year)
Salary: Support Staff Scale 18-23, dependent on experience
Recruitment: Exclusively managed by TimePlan Education

About the Role

TimePlan Education is exclusively sourcing an Executive Assistant on behalf of a secondary school in Stratford, East London.

This is an excellent opportunity for a highly organised, proactive and professional individual to provide high-quality administrative and organisational support to the Headteacher. Working closely with senior leaders, you will play a key role in supporting the school's leadership, governance and day-to-day operations.

The successful candidate will be confident managing competing priorities, handling confidential information and communicating professionally with staff, trustees, parents and external stakeholders.

Key Responsibilities
- Provide comprehensive administrative support to the Headteacher, including diary management, appointments, meetings and correspondence.
- Prepare agendas, reports, presentations and meeting documentation for senior leaders and trustees.
- Coordinate leadership meetings, school events and strategic planning activities.
- Maintain and monitor the school's policy schedule, ensuring policies are reviewed, updated and published within required deadlines.
- Maintain accurate records, databases and filing systems, ensuring confidentiality and GDPR compliance.
- Support governance arrangements, including the preparation of trustee meeting papers, agendas and minutes.
- Assist with audit preparation, compliance requirements and the monitoring of school improvement priorities.
- Act as a professional point of contact for senior leaders, trustees, visitors and external organisations.

The Ideal Candidate

The successful candidate will have:
- Previous experience in an executive assistant, personal assistant or senior administrative role.
- Excellent organisational and time-management skills, with the ability to manage multiple priorities and meet deadlines.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills.
- Excellent attention to detail and confidence preparing professional documents and reports.
- The ability to handle sensitive and confidential information with discretion.
- A proactive, flexible and professional approach, with the confidence to work with senior leaders and external stakeholders.
- Strong IT skills and experience maintaining accurate records and administrative systems.
- A commitment to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people.

Experience working within a school or educational setting would be advantageous.

What's on Offer?
- A permanent position within a secondary school in Stratford, East London.
- A term-time working pattern of 41 weeks per year.
- A salary on Support Staff Scale 18-23, depending on experience.
- The opportunity to work closely with the Headteacher and contribute to the effective running of the school.

Safeguarding and Equal Opportunities

The school is committed to safeguarding and promoting the welfare of children and young people. The successful applicant will be required to undertake an enhanced DBS check and all necessary pre-employment checks in line with Keeping Children Safe in Education.

How to Apply

If you have the relevant administrative experience, excellent organisational skills and are looking for your next opportunity within education, we would love to hear from you.

For further information or to apply, please contact TimePlan Education.

Kind regards,
The TimePlan Education Team

Graduate Sales Support Executive

Uxbridge Permanent Full-time

Looking for your first serious commercial career opportunity?

Are you a bright, ambitious graduate with some office, administration or customer service experience who is ready for a role where you can really learn, develop and become an important part of a business?

We are recruiting for an established and successful company in Uxbridge that is looking for someone with potential.

You don't need years of experience. What matters more is that you're switched-on, professional, naturally good with people and eager to learn.

.

You'll work closely with experienced team, supporting a portfolio of business customers and gradually develop a strong understanding of the complete commercial process from quotations and pricing through to orders, projects, purchasing, deliveries and customer account support.

For the right person, it's an excellent opportunity to build a long-term career within a commercial environment.

What will you be doing?

You'll become an important point of contact for customers and provide day-to-day support to the sales and account management team.

Your responsibilities will include:
- Building strong relationships with business customers and responding to their enquiries.
- Preparing quotations and pricing information.
- Managing customer orders from initial enquiry through to successful delivery.
- Helping with tenders, pricing exercises and customer proposals.
- Keeping customers informed and making sure they receive an excellent level of service.
- Coordinating with suppliers and internal departments to ensure orders run smoothly.
- Producing customer reports and analysing information using Excel.
- Maintaining accurate customer and CRM information.
- Investigating queries and finding solutions when things don't go according to plan.
- Learning about products, customers and the wider commercial operation.
- Taking on greater responsibility as your knowledge and confidence develop.

Who are we looking for?

We're particularly interested in candidates at the early stages of their career who can demonstrate genuine potential.

You could be a recent graduate with some office, retail, hospitality or customer-facing experience, or perhaps you're already working in your first commercial role and feel ready for something with greater development opportunities.

You'll ideally have:
- A degree or equivalent level of education.
- Some previous office, administration, customer service or commercial experience.
- Excellent communication skills and a confident telephone manner.
- A genuinely customer-focused approach.
- Strong attention to detail.
- Good numerical and analytical ability.
- Confidence using Microsoft Office, particularly Excel.
- The ability to organise your workload and manage several priorities.
- A proactive attitude you'll ask questions, use your initiative and want to understand how things work.
- The maturity and professionalism to communicate with business customers.

Most importantly, we're looking for someone who is bright, personable, curious and keen to progress.

You won't be expected to arrive knowing everything. You'll receive support while you learn the business, but you'll need the enthusiasm and ability to absorb information quickly and gradually take ownership.

Why consider this opportunity?

This could be a particularly good move if you've completed your degree and are now looking for a role that gives you genuine commercial experience rather than simply another administrative job.

You'll gain exposure to customer account management, sales, pricing, purchasing, projects and business operations while working alongside an experienced team.

There is plenty to learn and scope to develop as you prove yourself.

If you're ambitious, commercially curious and looking for an opportunity where your potential will be recognised, we'd really like to hear from you.

title: Human Resources Coordinator
description:
HR Coordinator EMEA Location: UK Hybrid working
Salary: Competitive, dependent on experience
Working hours: Monday Friday, 8:30am 5:30pm (37.5 hours per week)
Working pattern: 3 days in the office, 2 days working from home

The Opportunity An exciting opportunity has arisen for an experienced and motivated HR Coordinator to join the international HR team of a globally recognised, family-owned organisation with an established reputation for excellence.

This is a varied, hands-on HR generalist position supporting approximately 112 employees across EMEA, with some additional responsibility for the International region. Working within a small, collaborative HR team, you will play an important role in delivering effective HR operations, supporting recruitment activity and ensuring a positive employee experience throughout the employee lifecycle.

The role offers an excellent opportunity for someone with a strong administrative foundation and a broad HR background who is keen to develop their knowledge, take ownership of responsibilities and progress their career within an international business. CIPD qualification is desirable, and support for further professional study may be available.

Key Responsibilities
Recruitment & Talent Acquisition
- Coordinate recruitment activity from vacancy approval through to offer and onboarding, with a strong emphasis on direct sourcing and internal recruitment.
- Advise and support Line Managers on recruitment strategies, candidate sourcing and selection processes.
- Advertise vacancies and utilise LinkedIn and other recruitment platforms to identify and engage potential candidates.
- Review CVs, screen applications, qualify candidates and conduct initial conversations to assess suitability and cultural alignment.
- Coordinate interviews, manage candidate communications and maintain accurate recruitment records.
- Prepare offer letters and employment contracts and coordinate pre-employment checks.
- Organise onboarding and induction processes to ensure a smooth experience for new starters.

HR Administration & Employee Relations
- Provide comprehensive HR administration across the employee lifecycle, including onboarding, employee changes, absence management and offboarding.
- Maintain accurate employee records, personnel files and HR systems, ensuring compliance with GDPR requirements.
- Process employee updates and maintain data across relevant HR systems.
- Support performance reviews, salary and bonus reviews, training coordination and employee development activities.
- Administer annual leave, sickness absence and family-related leave processes.
- Assist with employee engagement initiatives and support meetings and one-to-ones with the HR Director where required.
- Produce HR reports, recruitment trackers and headcount information, ensuring data accuracy and timely reporting.
- Identify opportunities to improve processes and support wider HR projects.

Payroll, Pensions & Benefits
- Coordinate and support UK and European payroll processes, liaising with outsourced providers to ensure accurate and timely submissions.
- Assist with payroll changes, employee amendments and associated documentation.
- Administer employee benefits, including pensions, private medical and dental insurance, life assurance and income protection.
- Liaise with external brokers and benefits providers to manage queries and support day-to-day administration.
- Process pension enrolments and monthly administration, acting as a point of contact for employee enquiries.
- Support international benefits administration and ensure employee changes are accurately recorded.

title: Receptionist
description: Earl's Court Medical Centre has an exciting opportunity for a Medical Receptionist to join our welcoming and forward thinking Practice team on a part-time basis. Your normal pattern of working will be Monday - Friday, within the hours of 8am-6:30pm (5 hours per day). Interested applicants must have primary care and SystmOne experience. Key Responsibilities include: Greeting and assisting patients at the reception desk Managing appointments, cancellations and patients enquiries Answering telephone calls and directing queries appropriately Processing repeat prescription requests Supporting the administrative and clinical team with day-to-day tasks Maintaining confidentially and ensuring accurate record- keeping Processing ingoing and outgoing patient records This is a patient facing role that requires excellent communication skills, attention to detail, and a calm, efficient approach to working in a fast-paced environment. Reception duties: Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the Practice. Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. Explain Practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are completed. Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. Enter requests for home visits into the home visits book, ensuring careful recording of all relevant details and where necessary refer to Duty Doctor. Action repeat prescription requests and ensure that they are ready for collection by the patient within 72 hours, in line with Practice protocol. Take action on clinicians requests for further information/patient contact information etc. (including computerised practice notes), ensuring completion of all associated paperwork. Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non-General Medical Services) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. Enter patient information on to the computer as required. Prepare clinical rooms for surgeries, supply prescription forms and record numbers in use and ensure adequate supplies of consumables (including bottles, couch rolls, test request forms etc.). Premises: Open up premises at the start of the day when first to arrive, de-activate alarm and make all necessary preparations to receive patients. When last to leave at the end of the day, ensure that the building is totally secured, internal lights are off and the alarm activated. Ensure that all new patients are registered onto the computer system promptly and accurately Make and serve refreshments for meetings, ensure the kitchen is kept clean and tidy and air and tidy the waiting room in turn with other staff. Covering colleagues holiday and sick cover as required. Process incoming and outgoing mail according to practice protocols. Record actions taken in patient record where appropriate or in accordance with practice protocols. Complete other Daily/ Weekly and Monthly core tasks to support to smooth running of the reception area Any other administration duties as necessitated by the needs of the practice. Confidentiality : In the course of seeking treatment, patients entrust us with, or allow us to gather, sensitive information in relation to their health and other matters. They do so in confidence and have the right to expect that staff will respect their privacy and act appropriately. In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, Practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the Practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential. Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the Practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the Practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. Health & Safety: The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the Practice Health & Safety Policy, to include: Using personal security systems within the workplace according to Practice guidelines Identifying the risks involved in work activities and undertaking such activities in a way that manages those risks Making effective use of training to update knowledge and skills Using appropriate infection control procedures, maintaining work areas in a tidy and safe way and free from hazards Reporting potential risks identified Act as Chaperone when requested by clinician and in accordance with the Chaperone policy. Equality and Diversity: The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues, to include: Acting in a way that recognises the importance of peoples rights, interpreting them in a way that is consistent with the Practice policies and procedures, and current legislation Respecting the privacy, dignity, needs and beliefs of patients, carers and colleagues Behaving in a manner which is welcoming to the individual, is non-judgmental and respects their circumstances, feelings priorities and rights. Personal/Professional Development: The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the Practice as part of this employment, such training to include: Participation in an annual individual performance review, including taking responsibility for maintaining a record of their own personal and/or professional development Taking responsibility for their own development, learning and performance and demonstrating skills and activities to others who are undertaking similar work Quality : The post-holder will strive to maintain quality within the Practice, and will: Alert other team members to issues of quality and risk Assess own performance and take accountability for own actions, either directly or under supervision Contribute to the effectiveness of the team by reflecting on own and team activities and making suggestions on ways to improve and enhance the teams performance Work effectively with individuals in other agencies to meet patients needs Effectively manage own time, workload and resources Communication : The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise peoples needs for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly Contribution to the Implementation of Services: The post-holder will: Apply Practice policies, standards and guidance Discuss with other members of the team how the policies, standards and guidelines will affect own work Participate in audit where appropriate

title: Reception Administrator
description: The post holder's primary responsibility is to act as a Reception Admin to the Extended Access Service (EAS), QHS GP Care Home Service, and New Mill Street Surgery, based at Spa Medical Centre or New Mill Street Surgery. In addition the post holder will provide administrative support to other services provided by QHS, as agreed with the Service Manager. The EAS is a service, which opened in April 2015, where local GP practices who are members of QHS book their own patients in for either urgent (same day or next day) appointments or routine appointments. The post holder will be expected to liaise closely with member practices. The post holder will be expected to cover reception, meet and greet patients and handle their queries. It is the role of the Reception Administrator to assist the patients in the easiest possible way to see the GP/nurse or other health professional. Patient enquires must be handled courteously and efficiently and with an awareness of the needs of the patient. Accurate administration is important to ensure that the work of the practice is carried out efficiently and that complete records are maintained. Quay Health Solutions will accept applicants looking for part time and full time roles. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early should we receive a significant amount of applications. To provide patients who make contact with a QHS service with the best customer service. To answer the telephone promptly & deal with enquiries in a helpful & courteous manner, being aware of the need to maintain confidentiality at all times regarding patients & staff. To book, cancel & amend patient appointments using the clinical system & book patients in the appropriate service when needed using NHS Smartcard to trace patients on the Spine. To chaperone for patients & staff upon request. To identify any discrepancies in patient information received from practices & escalate appropriately. To deal with requests for assistance from doctors, nurses & other members of clinical team, including making calls to patients. To order ambulances & telephone interpreters for patients as required. To open & close the centre at the beginning & end of the day, checking security & setting the alarms. To adopt a proactive approach & deal with any issue relating to reception which may arise. Prioritising daily duties to ensure deadlines are met. To send referrals to the relevant services as requested by clinical staff & accurately document the receipt in patients records. To assist with monitoring & ordering of clinical & other supplies. To process the deductions for patients who have left the practice. Correctly labelling all outgoing medical records and marking them on EMIS. To act as a chaperone during LARC clinics when required, supporting the clinical team in the delivery of patient care. Please see the attached job description and person specification for all of the relevant information.

title: Receptionist
description: We are looking for 2 Recepetionists to join our team. Working 16.5 hours per week, shifts will vary from mornings and afternoons. MUST HAVE GP & EMIS EXPERIENCE. The Receptionist will support staff with the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with multidisciplinary team members and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers. The post-holder will be an integral part of the general practice team. Welcome patients and visitors in a professional, friendly, and courteous manner. Answer telephone calls promptly, deal with enquiries, take messages, and direct calls to the appropriate staff. Book, amend, and cancel appointments in accordance with practice procedures. Register new patients and update patient records, ensuring information is accurate and up to date. Manage patient enquiries face-to-face, by telephone, and via online communication systems. Handle confidential patient information in accordance with GDPR, confidentiality requirements, and practice policies. Process repeat prescription requests in line with practice procedures Liaise with GPs, nurses, healthcare professionals, and other members of the practice team to support the smooth running of the surgery. Signpost patients to appropriate services and healthcare professionals, following practice protocols. Deal with sensitive situations and patient complaints calmly, professionally, and with empathy. Follow practice policies and procedures relating to safeguarding, health and safety, infection prevention, and information governance. Maintain a clean, tidy, and welcoming reception area. Undertake any other reasonable duties to support the effective day-to-day running of the practice. To provide a professional, friendly, and efficient reception service to patients, visitors, and healthcare professionals, ensuring the smooth day-to-day running of the GP practice. The postholder will support the clinical and administrative teams while maintaining patient confidentiality and delivering a high standard of customer service.

title: Receptionist

The practice is situated in a pleasant part of Blackheath in South East London with good transport links and local shops. The position is for 22 hours per week over four days, based on a seven week rolling rota. Please note that the rota is variable and you will be working different days over a seven week period. This is based on a 7am start and 12.30pm finish 8am start and 1pm finish, 1pm start and 6pm finish, 1.30pm start with a 7pm finish. This can vary , depending on the needs of the practice during sickness and annual leave. Flexibility is essential. Saturday mornings are part of our enhanced access service and there is the option to work these sessions on a rotation basis. We are a friendly team, who are supportive of each other and there will be opportunity to develop new skills. Duties include: Covering reception desk, answering telephone calls, booking appointments via AccuRx triage system, dealing with patient queries, order prescriptions, process admin duties for clinical staff, general administration such as filing and liaising with other health care providers in a professional manner, and processing clinical letters through the Docman system. The duties are variable, depending on what is required on the day. Candidates must have strong communication skills, be friendly, reliable and willing to learn. The applicant must have the ability to prioritise workload. Applicants must have the ability to work within a team, have experience of EMIS, AccuRx and Docman and IT skills. Previous experience of working in General Practice is essential, further training will be available for any candidates that show a passion for learning. Job Description Main duties include: Covering reception desk greeting patients and visitors with a professional and friendly manner. Manage the booking system efficiently, signposting patients to the relevant services. Answering incoming calls, respond to queries and manage email correspondence promptly. Assist clinicians as needed, including handling paperwork, stocking consultation rooms and daily end of day duties to ensure the rooms are meeting infection control standards. Manage office supplies, handling incoming/outgoing post and perform general administrative duties. Maintain accurate patient records and ensure confidentiality. Candidates must have strong communication skills, be friendly, reliable and willing to learn and develop their skills.In the performance of the duties outlined in this Job Description, the post-holder may have access to confidential information relating to patients and their carers, practice staff and other healthcare workers. They may also have access to information relating to the practice as a business organisation. All such information from any source is to be regarded as strictly confidential Information relating to patients, carers, colleagues, other healthcare workers or the business of the practice may only be divulged to authorised persons in accordance with the practice policies and procedures relating to confidentiality and the protection of personal and sensitive data. The post-holder will assist in promoting and maintaining their own and others health, safety and security as defined in the practice Health & Safety Policy. The post-holder will support the equality, diversity and rights of patients, carers and colleagues. The post-holder will participate in any training programme implemented by the practice as part of this employment. The post-holder should recognise the importance of effective communication within the team and will strive to: Communicate effectively with other team members Communicate effectively with patients and carers Recognise needs of people for alternative methods of communication and respond accordingly.

title: Receptionist/Administrator
description: The Pinner Road Surgery is a friendly, forward-thinking GP practice in Harrow. We are seeking a committed, enthusiastic and IT-confident individual to join our reception team. You will be the first point of contact for our patients, providing professional and courteous support to both patients and staff. Excellent communication and customer service skills are essential. Experience in a healthcare setting is desirable but not essential. Full training will be provided. As a Receptionist, you will be the first point of contact for our patients and visitors. Your responsibilities will include providing administrative support to the clinical and non-clinical teams, coordinating front-desk activities, greeting patients, handling telephone queries, and managing correspondence. Main Duties of the Job would include: Greet and direct patients and visitors Book, amend and cancel appointments via EMIS Web Manage patient registrations (new, temporary and updates) Handle incoming calls and manage the practice email inbox Process incoming/outgoing mail and documentation Scan, file and input patient-related data into EMIS Web Support administrative requests from clinical staff Respect and maintain patient confidentiality at all times To be responsible for undertaking a wide range of reception and administrative duties and the provision of general support to the multidisciplinary team. Duties can include but are not limited to, greeting and directing patients, patient registration, booking appointments, processing of information (electronic and hard copy) and assisting patients as required. To act as the central point of contact for patients, the distribution of information, messages and enquiries for the clinical team, liaising with multidisciplinary team members and external agencies such as secondary care and community service providers.

title: Team Administrator
company: South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
advertiser_name: South London and Maudsley NHS Foundation Trust
description: The post holder will provide administrative and operational support to the Mental Health Liaison Team, contributing to the effective delivery of services across acute hospital settings. They will support the coordination and tracking of referrals, maintain accurate patient records on EPJS and other systems, and ensure compliance with Trust and information governance requirements. The role involves liaising with a range of internal and external stakeholders, effective communication and the timely completion of administrative processes. The post holder will also assist with patient flow and bed management and deputise for the Patient Flow Coordinator during periods of absence or increased service demand, helping to facilitate safe and timely admissions, transfers, and discharges. Acting as a key point of contact between liaison teams, Emergency Departments, inpatient wards, bed management teams, community services, and external providers, you will support the management of mental health bed demand. Duties include coordinating Mental Health Act assessment referrals, processing bed requests, assisting with documentation, arranging transport, maintaining tracking systems, monitoring delays, and supporting service improvement activities. The successful candidate will have excellent organisational, communication, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work independently, prioritise workloads, and contribute to the delivery of safe, effective, and high-quality patient care. Provide administrative and operational support to the Mental Health Liaison Team, including referral coordination, patient flow support, and assistance with discharge planning. Maintain accurate patient records on EPJS and Trust systems, process clinical documentation, and support data collection, reporting, and audits. Act as a key point of contact for patients, carers, staff, and partner agencies, ensuring effective communication and escalation of urgent issues. Liaise with hospital, community, and external services to support continuity of care and maintain administrative tracking systems. Undertake general administrative duties, including diary management, meeting support, minute taking, filing, and correspondence. Contribute to governance, quality improvement, training, and service development activities, while providing reception and cross-site cover as required. As outlined above, this role requires that the post holder provide comprehensive administrative, operational and patient flow support.
