title: GP Receptionist
description: Join Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group as a full-time GP Receptionist, primarily based at Heathway Medical Centre in Dagenham. You will be a welcoming first point of contact for patients and a valued member of our friendly and supportive practice team. We are looking for someone reliable, organised and confident communicating with people face to face. Previous GP reception experience is an advantage, but not essential. We also welcome applicants with strong customer service experience who enjoy helping people, can manage a variety of tasks and are quick to learn new online systems. Good IT skills, excellent communication and a friendly, professional approach are essential. This is a fixed-term position until 8 August 2027, with the possibility of extension. The role is 37.5 hours per week, working varied shifts between 07:45 and 18:30, Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. Pay is £12.71 per hour. Our wider practice group offers opportunities to gain experience, develop new skills and apply for permanent positions as vacancies arise. We reserve the right to close this vacancy early if sufficient applications are received. Early applications are encouraged. As a GP Receptionist, you will play an important role in supporting patients and helping the practice run smoothly. Your daily responsibilities will include: Welcoming patients and visitors, providing friendly and professional assistance. Responding to patient enquiries face to face, by telephone and through online systems. Helping patients access appropriate services, including assisting with online appointment requests. Using our clinical system (EMIS Web) and other digital platforms to manage patient information and administrative tasks. Processing patient requests, including prescriptions, test-related enquiries and general correspondence. Supporting GPs, nurses and other team members with day-to-day administrative duties. Maintaining accurate records and handling confidential information appropriately. Working closely with colleagues to provide a positive experience for patients. Full training and guidance on our practice systems and procedures will be provided. We value teamwork, initiative and a willingness to learn. Job Description GP Receptionist Organisation: Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group Primary Location: Heathway Medical Centre, Dagenham Contract: Full-time, fixed-term until 8 August 2027, with the possibility of extension Hours: 37.5 hours per week, with varied shifts between 07:45 and 18:30, Monday to Friday, excluding bank holidays. To provide a friendly, professional and efficient reception and administrative service to patients, visitors and healthcare professionals. The GP Receptionist plays an important role in supporting patients to access healthcare services, maintaining accurate records and assisting the wider practice team with daily operations. The successful candidate will be based primarily at Heathway Medical Centre, with occasional cover at other practices within Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group where required. 1. Patient Reception and Customer Service Welcome patients and visitors in a friendly, helpful and professional manner. Act as a first point of contact for patients attending the practice. Respond to patient enquiries face to face, by telephone and through digital communication systems. Assist patients with appointment requests and provide information about available services. Support patients who may require additional assistance accessing healthcare services. Communicate clearly and sensitively with patients from different backgrounds and with varying needs. Handle patient concerns and difficult situations calmly, professionally and respectfully, referring matters to senior colleagues when appropriate. Maintain a welcoming, organised and professional reception environment. 2. Appointment Management and Patient Access Support patients with accessing appointments and services in accordance with practice procedures. Assist patients in using online consultation and appointment request systems. Provide guidance on accessing the NHS App and other available digital services. Process appointment requests, cancellations and changes as directed by practice procedures. Signpost patients to appropriate services using established practice guidance and care navigation procedures. Escalate urgent concerns or clinical queries to the appropriate healthcare professional without providing clinical advice. Help ensure patients receive clear and accurate information about practice services. 3. Clinical Systems and Digital Administration Use EMIS Web and other practice systems to access and update patient information accurately. Process patient requests received through online platforms and electronic communication systems. Scan, upload and attach relevant documents to patient records. Record patient interactions and administrative activities appropriately. Support the processing of incoming correspondence and electronic documents. Maintain accurate records while following confidentiality and information governance requirements. Learn and confidently use new digital systems as introduced by the practice. 4. General Administrative Duties Process routine patient enquiries relating to prescriptions, test requests, referrals and other practice services in accordance with established procedures. Assist with the collection and distribution of forms, letters and other documents. Support the preparation and processing of administrative correspondence. Liaise with hospitals, pharmacies, community healthcare providers and other external organisations when required. Maintain accurate records and ensure administrative tasks are completed in a timely manner. Support clinical and non-clinical colleagues with general administrative tasks. Assist with maintaining an organised and efficient reception and office environment. 5. Teamwork and Communication Work collaboratively with reception colleagues, GPs, nurses, healthcare assistants and administrative staff. Communicate effectively with colleagues to support the smooth running of the practice. Provide reception cover and assistance to colleagues when required. Share relevant information with appropriate team members to ensure continuity of service. Participate in team meetings, training and development activities. Contribute positively to a respectful, supportive and professional working environment. 6. Confidentiality, Safety and Professional Standards Maintain strict patient confidentiality and comply with data protection and information governance requirements. Follow practice policies and procedures, including safeguarding, health and safety, infection prevention and control, and equality and diversity. Recognise and appropriately escalate safeguarding concerns or situations requiring clinical attention. Treat all patients, visitors and colleagues with dignity, respect and sensitivity. Work within the boundaries of the receptionist role and seek guidance when necessary. Maintain professional standards of conduct and appearance. Full induction and training on practice-specific systems and procedures will be provided. Previous experience in a GP practice and familiarity with EMIS Web would be advantageous but are not essential. We welcome candidates with experience in customer-facing roles who demonstrate strong communication skills, a positive attitude, good computer skills and a willingness to learn. As part of Dr Sharma & Rai Practice Group, employees may have opportunities to develop additional skills, gain experience across different practice functions and apply for permanent vacancies as they arise. The successful candidate must be flexible in their working hours and available for different shifts within the practice's core opening hours. This job description outlines the main responsibilities of the position and may be reviewed or adapted to meet the operational needs of the practice, within the appropriate scope of the role.

title: GP Receptionist
description: Join our friendly team at St Katharine Docks Practice , a welcoming single-handed GP surgery set in the beautiful surroundings of St Katharine Docks, just moments from the Tower of London. We pride ourselves on providing high-quality, personalised care to our patients and creating a supportive, professional, and inclusive workplace. We are looking for a Receptionist to provide cover , helping to ensure the smooth running of our busy front desk. As the first point of contact for patients, youll play a vital role in making every patient feel welcome, listened to, and supported. Youll handle calls, manage appointments, process correspondence, and assist the GP and wider team in delivering excellent service. This role is ideal for someone who enjoys helping others, communicates clearly and kindly, and can stay calm under pressure. Youll need to be organised, confident using computers, and committed to maintaining confidentiality at all times. In return, we offer a friendly working environment, on-the-job training, and opportunities for personal development. Youll be part of a small, close-knit team where your contribution truly makes a difference to the lives of our patients and the success of our practice. If youre reliable, compassionate, and looking for a rewarding role in the heart of London, wed love to hear from you. Welcome and assist patients and visitors in person and over the telephone in a professional and friendly manner. Manage incoming calls, respond to general enquiries, and direct calls as appropriate. Schedule and manage patient appointments using the practice clinical system - EMIS Web. Register new patients and update existing patient information accurately. Handle incoming and outgoing post and emails. Obtain external medical reports, test results, and other documentation as required. Scan and file correspondence and clinical documents. Maintain a tidy, organised, and welcoming reception area. Safeguard patient confidentiality and comply with GDPR and NHS data protection requirements. Provide reassurance and support to patients, maintaining a calm and caring approach. Carry out general administrative duties as required by the GP or Practice Manager. Ensure an effective and efficient reception service is provided to patients and any other visitors to the Practice. Deal with all general enquiries, explain procedures and make new and follow-up appointments. Using your own judgment and communication skills ensure that patients with no prior appointment but who need urgent consultation are seen in a logical and non-disruptive manner. Explain Practice arrangements and formal requirements to new patients and those seeking temporary cover and ensure procedures are completed. Receive and make telephone calls as required. Divert calls and take messages, ensuring accuracy of detail and prompt appropriate delivery. Enter requests for home visits into the home visits book, ensuring careful recording of all relevant details and where necessary refer to Duty Doctor. Action repeat prescription requests and ensure that they are ready for collection by the patient within 48 hours, in line with Practice protocol. Take action on clinicians requests for further information/patient contact information etc. including computerised practice notes, ensuring completion of all associated paperwork. Advise patients of relevant charges for private (non-General Medical Services) services, accept payment and issue receipts for same. Enter patient information on to the computer as required. Prepare clinical rooms for surgeries, supply prescription forms and record numbers in use and ensure adequate supplies of consumables - including bottles, couch rolls, test request forms etc..

title: GP Receptionist / Administrator
description: Part-Time GP Receptionist/Administrator We are looking for an experienced, part-time GP Receptionist/Administrator to join our friendly and busy team. The successful candidate will be organised, calm under pressure, confident on the telephone, and able to work independently as well as part of a team. Previous experience in a GP practice is preferred, along with good administrative skills and a commitment to providing a helpful, professional and compassionate service to our patients. This is a permanent, part-time position with the following working hours: Monday to Thursday: 12:30 pm 6:30 pm Friday: 8:30 am 6:30 pm Flexibility to cover colleagues annual leave is also required. We are looking for someone reliable and enthusiastic who would like to become a valued, long-term member of our team. Providing front-desk reception and dealing with patient queries. Answering telephone calls and booking appointments. Supporting the GP on duty with triage administration. Actioning online requests and following up queries. Managing clinical documents. Carrying out general administrative duties. Working independently and as part of a team. Maintaining patient confidentiality at all times. Prioritising workload and remaining calm in a busy environment. Key Responsibilities and Requirements The role involves providing front-desk reception services, answering telephone calls, responding to patient queries, booking appointments and supporting the GP on duty with triage administration. The successful candidate will be organised, reliable and able to work independently as well as part of a team. They will be confident in prioritising their workload, managing competing demands and remaining calm and professional in a busy environment, while maintaining strict patient confidentiality at all times. Previous experience in a GP practice is preferred, particularly familiarity with EMIS Web, Accurx, Docman and the ERS referral system . Good communication, administrative and organisational skills, together with a friendly and professional approach to patient care, are essential.

title: Medical Receptionist
description: The Law Medical Group Practice is seeking a reliable and organised Receptionist to join the team at its Wembley branch. The practice is committed to delivering high quality primary care services to its local community and ensuring smooth day to day patient flow through efficient administrative and reception support. The successful candidate will play a key role in supporting the clinical and non clinical teams by undertaking a range of front of house and administrative duties. This will include managing appointments through EMIS, handling patient queries, processing incoming correspondence and ensuring information is accurately directed to the relevant clinicians in a timely manner. The role will involve full front of house responsibilities, including welcoming and directing patients, responding to queries and providing a professional and efficient service both in person and over the telephone. Working Pattern: Part Time, 27.5 Hours per Week The working hours are Monday to Friday, 1:00 pm to 6:30 pm. Please note: The working days and hours are non negotiable . Applicants must be able to commit to this working pattern. Eligibility: Applicants must be UK citizens and have a minimum of five years of work experience in the UK. The role involves providing comprehensive reception support to the multidisciplinary team within the practice. Key responsibilities include managing patient interactions, handling incoming correspondence, and ensuring accurate distribution of information to clinicians. The position includes front-desk duties such as greeting and directing patients, managing the appointment system using EMIS , booking appointments, responding to patient enquiries, and supporting the smooth and efficient day-to-day operation of the practice. The following are the core responsibilities of the Administrator/Receptionist . There may occasionally be a requirement to carry out other duties depending on workload, operational needs, and staffing levels. Primary Responsibilities Receive and process correspondence from hospitals, external healthcare providers, and other agencies. Scan and upload documents onto the EMIS clinical system, ensuring accurate patient record management. Review and appropriately allocate documents within EMIS , forwarding them to the relevant clinician for review and action. Initiate and respond to requests from patients, practice staff, and external healthcare agencies in a professional and timely manner. Photocopy and prepare documentation as required by clinicians and practice staff. Provide cover for colleagues during periods of absence to ensure continuity of service. Accurately input patient information and updates into EMIS where required. Manage and resolve patient queries efficiently, escalating issues where appropriate. Maintain a clean, organised, and efficient reception environment at all times. Support the clinical team with day-to-day operational tasks as required. Complete tasks relating to patient results, correspondence, and clinical letters where appropriate. Demonstrate flexibility and adaptability in managing changing workloads and priorities to ensure the smooth operation of the practice. Use EMIS and other digital systems effectively for patient record management, appointment scheduling, and internal communication. Secondary Responsibilities In addition to the primary responsibilities, the Medical Receptionist may also be required to: Maintain and monitor the practice appointment system using EMIS . Process appointment requests received in person, by telephone, and via online systems. Answer incoming telephone calls and direct them appropriately or deal with enquiries where possible. Signpost patients to the appropriate healthcare professional or NHS service. Support practice audits and administrative reviews as directed by management. Process incoming electronic communications and documents where required. Scan and attach patient-related documentation accurately to patient records within EMIS . Carry out opening and closing procedures in accordance with the practice rota and operational requirements.

title: Personal Assistant
description: As Personal Assistant (PA) to the Patient Experience Director (PED) the post holder will provide comprehensive administrative and business support, ensuring the Director's responsibilities are effectively managed. This includes managing a complex diary, correspondence, communication, coordination and delegation ensuring the Director receives a consistent and high-level of support. The post holder will work closely with key colleagues and the senior leadership team to the Director. They will play a crucial role in ensuring the smooth and efficient operation of the Director's office, enabling the Director to focus on their extensive core responsibilities. As PA you will need to be confident to self-initiate tasks, be a clear communicator and comfortable operating efficiently and effectively in a high-pressure environment. Please be aware that should you be successful in this position, you will be hired to the job title of Personal Assistant, and this job title is advertised to attract the right skills needed for the role. We are looking for an experienced personal assistant who is a strong team player, highly organised, and who has the ability to communicate effectively and professionally with a wide range of people. Your duties will include but not limited to; Complex diary and mailbox management Meeting coordination Travel arrangements Monitoring and recording of annual leave/absences Entering expense claims for Director Respond to ad-hoc, non-routine requests by the Director and their direct reports effectively, professionally and in good time. Meetings/events are held across various sites therefore some flexibility is required. Detailed job description and main responsibilities Key responsibilities as PA to Director; Diary Management: Managing a complex diary, balancing competing priorities, and coordinating travel arrangements. Meeting Coordination: Preparing agendas, taking minutes, and following up on action items. Correspondence: Handling internal and external communications, including emails and written correspondence. Information Dissemination: Ensuring accurate and timely dissemination of information to relevant parties. Administrative Support: Providing general administrative support, such as filing, data entry, and photocopying. Team Support: Supporting other administrative staff and providing assistance when needed. Confidentiality: Maintaining confidentiality of sensitive information. Communication and Interpersonal Skills: Effectively communicating with a wide range of individuals, both internally and externally. Organisation and Time Management: Managing workload effectively, prioritising tasks, and meeting deadlines. You can find further details about the role, including key responsibilities and accountabilities, alongside the organisational structure and person specification in the attached Job Description and other supporting documents. Secondments Applicants from within the NHS will be offered on a secondment basis only, agreement should be obtained from their employer prior to submitting the application.

title: Clinical Administrator
description: The Gender Identity Clinic (GIC) is the longest established clinic of its kind in the world (1966), and consists of a large multidisciplinary team, with whom the post holder will work. It accepts self-referrals, as well as referrals from primary or secondary care of adults who are gender diverse or dysphoric. Care includes specialist assessment and, where necessary, diagnosis of gender incongruence, and may also include psychological therapies, speech & language therapy, endocrinology, referral for hair removal, referral for surgical procedures and aftercare. We are looking for an experienced Administrator to join and support the Adult Gender Identity Clinic (GIC). Candidates must demonstrate their ability to support aspects of our clinical work. The suitable candidate is required to provide effective and efficient administration support to our clinical services by ensuring a high standard of data entry, and by making the best use of our system resources. The post holder will need to be confident in managing busy emails systems from clinicians, managers, and internal and external stakeholders. Within this busy and stimulating clinical team the position will require you to have excellent communication and organisational skills as well as enjoying working within a team setting. The candidate should be able to demonstrate the ability to work as a member of a functional, task-based team, and can ensure they can communicate and liaise with administrative colleagues, patients, family members, external professionals and with clinical practitioners. This should also include evidence of high-quality skills where attention to detail, strong IT skills and accurate patient data entry skills is essential and demonstrating the ability to use your initiative and prioritise your own workload. Having experience of using Carenotes our electronic patient record is desirable. Candidates are requested to use the section "Supporting Information" on the application form to set out their reasons for applying and their suitability, referring to the person specification, for this post. Please see the attached job description and person specification for more details of the role and requirements of the vacancy.

title: GP Receptionist
description: We are offering an exciting opportunity to join our hardworking and welcoming GP Practice as a Receptionist, providing vital support and becoming an integral part of our dedicated Team. This is a part-time position, working 5 shifts per week (5.75 hours each), Monday to Friday, with a mix of morning and afternoon schedules. In this part-time role, no two days are ever the same youll be helping patients, solving problems, and making a real difference in peoples lives. Alongside greeting patients, managing appointments, and handling enquiries with care, youll also take on some important administrative tasks that keep the practice running smoothly. It can be challenging at times, but youll be part of a team that works together, supports one another, and takes pride in delivering excellent patient care. This role comes with full training, so no formal qualifications are required. However, previous experience in a GP practice would be preferential but what matters most is your enthusiasm, reliability, and willingness to learn. What you will be doing day to day As a GP Receptionist, you will be at the heart of our practice, making a real difference to patients and the team. Your role will be varied, rewarding, and sometimes challenging - but always important. Be the first friendly face and voice patients encounter, whether welcoming them in person, answering the phone, or responding to emails. Help patients feel supported by managing appointments, processing referrals, and guiding them through their healthcare journey. Keep communication flowing between patients and healthcare professionals, ensuring everyone has the information they need. Take on key admin tasks that keep the practice running smoothly, from handling queries to maintaining accurate records. Champion safety and standards by following procedures, keeping the environment clean and safe, and supporting governance responsibilities. Work closely with the Deputy Practice Manager to deliver excellent reception and administrative services, contributing to patient care and the wider success of the practice. This is a role where youll be helping people every day, working in a supportive team, and knowing that your contribution truly makes a difference. What youll be doing As a GP Receptionist, youll be the first point of contact for patients and play a key role in keeping the practice running smoothly. Your work will be varied, rewarding, and always important. Welcome patients and visitors in person, on the phone, and by email, making sure they feel supported. Book, change, or cancel appointments and help patients with referrals. Guide patients to the right healthcare professional or service. Arrange home visits when needed and follow simple triage steps. Keep the reception area clean and safe so patients feel comfortable. Spot and report problems to the Deputy Practice Manager. Help improve systems by checking processes and following health and safety rules. Protect patient privacy and treat everyone with dignity and respect. Join team meetings and share ideas to improve patient care. Handle concerns or complaints calmly and kindly. Act as a chaperone when patients need support during appointments. Keep accurate records of patient interactions. Register new patients and update records. Scan and process documents and use clinical IT systems. Use resources wisely and avoid unnecessary waste.

title: Medical Receptionist

title: Practice Administrator
description: We are looking for an organised, motivated and proactive individual to join The Wapping Group Practice and take the lead in managing our QOF, LES and patient recall systems. This is a temporary maternity cover position, with a fixed-term contract of at least 13 months. Flexible working hours: 25 to 37.5 hours per week . This is an important role within our practice, ensuring patients receive the care they need while helping us achieve our clinical and contractual targets. You will work closely with our clinical, administrative and PCN teams to coordinate recalls, monitor performance, improve processes and ensure accurate clinical coding. We offer a friendly and supportive working environment where you will have the opportunity to take ownership of your work, develop your skills and make a real difference to patient care and practice performance. We will provide the necessary training and support to help you succeed in this role, so you do not need to have experience in every aspect of the job. We are looking for someone who is willing to learn, takes initiative and is committed to delivering high-quality work. The successful candidate will be responsible for overseeing the practice's QOF, LES and patient recall systems, ensuring patients are contacted, booked and followed up appropriately. The role involves monitoring performance against clinical targets, coordinating recall activities with the administrative and PCN teams, managing appointment availability and ensuring accurate clinical coding on EMIS. You will also oversee childhood immunisation and cervical screening recalls, identify areas for improvement and work closely with the clinical team to maximise practice performance. Key Responsibilities QOF, LES and Target Management Manage and coordinate all QOF, LES and other contractual recall activities to ensure the practice achieves maximum performance against targets. Monitor QOF and LES dashboards regularly, identifying areas where performance needs improvement. Take responsibility for managing all targets comprehensively, ensuring patients are recalled, booked and appropriately coded. Regularly update EMIS searches and review performance dashboards to identify outstanding work and missed opportunities. Work closely with the clinical and administrative teams to ensure all targets are achieved within the required deadlines. Patient Recall Management Manage the practice's recall system from start to finish, ensuring eligible patients are identified, contacted, booked and followed up. Generate, distribute and monitor recall lists, ensuring work is completed accurately and on time. Allocate recall lists to PCN recall staff, monitor their progress and follow up on outstanding tasks. Ensure patients who do not respond to initial recall attempts are followed up appropriately. Send validation letters to patients who have not responded after repeated contact attempts, in line with practice protocols. Ensure accurate records are maintained of all recall attempts, patient responses and outcomes. Clinical Appointment Management Review and adjust clinical appointment sessions on EMIS, adding or removing appointment slots where necessary to support QOF and LES recall activities. Ensure sufficient clinical appointments are available for patients requiring reviews, monitoring, vaccinations and other target-related activities. Liaise with clinicians and the management team to plan appointment capacity according to recall demand and outstanding targets. Clinical Coding and Data Quality Ensure all QOF and LES activities are accurately coded on EMIS to support correct reporting and achievement. Identify missing or incorrect clinical codes and liaise with the relevant clinicians to resolve any issues. Provide training and guidance to administrative and recall staff on correct clinical coding procedures. Keep staff updated on changes to QOF, LES and other relevant coding requirements. Carry out regular data quality checks to ensure completed clinical activities are correctly recorded and reflected in performance reports. Childhood Immunisations and Cervical Screening Manage childhood immunisation recalls and targets, ensuring eligible children are identified, contacted and followed up. Monitor childhood immunisation performance and work with the clinical team to improve uptake and achieve contractual targets. Manage cervical screening recalls comprehensively, ensuring eligible patients are invited, booked and appropriately followed up. Monitor cervical screening uptake and identify patients who are overdue or have not responded to invitations. Ensure cervical screening records are accurately maintained, including coding of colposcopy correspondence and relevant clinical outcomes. Ensure cervical screening referral information is correctly recorded and processed through CSMS where required. Work closely with the clinical team to resolve coding discrepancies and ensure screening activity is accurately reflected in EMIS and performance dashboards. Staff Coordination and Training Coordinate the work of PCN recall staff by allocating tasks, setting priorities and monitoring progress. Provide regular feedback and guidance to ensure recall activities are completed efficiently. Train staff on recall procedures, EMIS searches, clinical coding and changes to contractual requirements. Maintain effective communication between clinical, administrative and PCN teams to ensure a coordinated approach to achieving practice targets. Identify areas for improvement and implement changes to strengthen recall processes and overall performance. Performance Monitoring and Reporting Regularly review QOF, LES, childhood immunisation and cervical screening performance. Identify gaps in achievement and take proactive steps to improve performance before contractual deadlines. Provide regular progress updates to the Practice Manager, highlighting outstanding targets, risks and areas requiring additional support. Ensure the practice maximises appropriate contractual achievement and income through effective recall management, accurate coding and timely completion of clinical activities.

title: GP Receptionist
description: Woodlands Medical Practice is a friendly, 5 partner GP practice in Sutton-in-Ashfield with approximately 11,500 patients. We obtained an Outstanding rating with the CQC and we are committed to providing patient-centred care in a happy, supportive and well-organised working environment. We are looking to recruit a part time Receptionist to join our team. The ideal candidates will be reliable with a flexible can do attitude to work. They will be highly motivated and able to work under pressure to deadlines and must be able to demonstrate exceptional customer service skills.
